title: Additive stabilized Postnikov entries
statement: Let A and B be abelian categories, and suppose D(A) is a derived category with its standard t-structure. For any PostnikovPageData P, there exists PostnikovStableData P: on the full subcategory where finite cycles and boundaries eventually stabilize at a fixed bidegree, the stabilized entries are additive functors, their late-page isomorphisms are natural and commute with the next-page homology projection. The witness interfaces are defined in [def-per-postnikov-additive-witness-data].

source.place: Tags 011T and 012U: cycles and boundaries and stationary-page quotients; morphism additivity follows from uniqueness of restriction and descent.

proof.text: Choose at each object a finite stationarity cutoff, and take the cokernel of the stationary boundary inclusion into stationary cycles. Every later cycle-tower projection is epi with that kernel, so gives a unique quotient isomorphism to the late page. Couple maps preserve finite cycles and boundaries; choose a common later cutoff for a pair and descend the restricted initial E-map to the stationary quotient. Cancellation proves cutoff independence, identities, composition and addition, and the successor-projection equation proves transition compatibility. Uses [def-sp-convergence], [lem-sp-derived-couple-functoriality]. Once cycles stop shrinking, cycleLift followed by the outgoing kernel inclusion is the old epimorphic projection composed with an isomorphism. The kernel inclusion is therefore epi and mono, hence invertible, and cycleLift is epi. This proves the final transition equation by epic cancellation.
